source_title: Official opening, embedded in the competition page
claim_context: The opening describes household installation, repair and maintenance across appliances and home services. Examples include fragmented water-purifier installation, disagreement between a tenant and landlord, repeated technician follow-ups, and service-contract coordination. Its suggested foundation is an automatically assembled service history, with an agent pursuing work to completion despite closed brand systems. These are the organiser's starting observations, not findings your team can claim to have discovered. [Official opening, embedded in the competition page](https://the-ken.com/case-competition-2026/).
access_notes: Direct public HTML or web retrieval; no sandbox execution. Prototype content read, not interactively tested.

claim_context: The Ken's official 2025 announcement names IIM Ahmedabad's A-Team as winner. Their concept moved suitable care from hospital to home through AI coordination and episode pricing. The organiser explicitly credited system-level thinking about alternatives, incentives, risks and dependencies. This supports a strategy centred on the whole service episode rather than a catalogue of AI features. [The Ken's winner announcement](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/the-ken_after-three-months-of-battle-indian-institute-activity-7407381828422074369-iPxl).

claim_context: **Check alternatives early.** Urban Company's Hyderabad microwave page describes inspection and quote approval, parts sourcing, workshop servicing where needed and post-repair warranty. These capabilities make a generic booking-and-chasing pitch weak. They do not establish that every customer's coordination problem is solved. [Urban Company: Hyderabad microwave repair](https://www.urbancompany.com/hyderabad-microwave-repair).

claim_context: The public showcase links prototype websites. Review of downloaded site content, rather than interactive testing or slide decks, found that ArogyaGhar.ai presents hospital and patient views, a staged care journey, consent, episode economics and exception handling. FinVaani presents a focused vernacular-investor journey using voice and visual guidance. The useful lesson is to make a specific user's job and decision boundaries tangible. Prototype testimonials, partner badges and projected outcomes were not independently verified. claim_context: P3P documents delegated agent payments using mandates and scoped payment tokens, with receipts. Its SDK documentation describes Grantex consent, scopes, transaction limits and budget handling. Therefore, "let an agent pay under a cap" is already a documented capability, not a defensible missing-capability claim. [P3P overview](https://www.pinelabs.com/docs/online-payments/ai/p3p); [P3P SDKs](https://www.pinelabs.com/docs/online-payments/ai/p3p/sdks).
